questions.q: What does the `with` statement do when opening a file?
options: Opens the file in append mode only
Automatically converts the file to CSV format
Guarantees the file is closed automatically when the block ends, even if an error occurs inside it
Prevents the file from ever being modified
questions.explain: Without with, you'd have to remember to call f.close() on every exit path, including error paths.

questions.q: What happens if you open an existing file with mode "w" and write to it?
options: The file's existing contents are completely overwritten
Your new content is added to the end of the existing contents
Python refuses to open the file
The file is opened read-only and the write is ignored
questions.explain: "w" mode creates the file if needed and overwrites it entirely if it already exists; "a" is for appending.

questions.q: In this lesson's orders.csv, what did iterating the raw text lines reveal about row 1005?
options: It has an extra column no other row has
It's a duplicate of row 1001
Its customer_name field is empty
Its quantity field is negative
questions.explain: Splitting line 1005 on commas and checking the customer_name field shows an empty string — a real missing value.

questions.q: Why is calling .readlines() on a very large file potentially a problem?
options: It loads every line into memory at once, which doesn't scale to multi-gigabyte files
It only works on files with a .csv extension
It automatically deletes the file after reading it
It can only read the first 21 lines of any file
questions.explain: Iterating the file object directly reads one line at a time instead of holding the whole file in memory.

questions.q: Why does a naive `line.strip().split(",")` approach break down on some real CSV files, even though it worked on this one?
options: It never breaks down — this is actually a fully reliable way to parse any CSV
strip() deletes numeric fields
split(",") only works on files with exactly one header row
If a field's value itself contains a comma, the split cuts that field in two and shifts every later column out of alignment
questions.explain: Real CSV fields that contain commas are quoted, and a plain split doesn't know to respect those quotes — which is why the csv module exists.
